subject: Ephemeral log access exception for production incident
messages:
From: SRE Oncall <sre-oncall@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-lead@acmeanalytics.com
Date: 2026-10-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Debug access request: ephemeral logs for transaction failures

Hi Marcus,

We are seeing a spiking error rate for a small subset of requests routed to your LLM endpoint (customer: Acme Analytics). Our SREs captured a short KV/trace segment that could explain why some requests are hitting a rare cache-invalidation path. The logs we need live in an ephemeral buffer with a 24-hour retention window and appear to have rotated out.

Can Redwood provide a short-term exception to retention so we can preserve and access the traces? We only need a 48-hour window backfilled (read-only) to pull the trace and redact customer identifiers.

Attached: trace_segment_20261002.json (partial), access-request-form.pdf (signed by Acme ops).

Thanks,
Maya Patel
SRE Oncall, Acme Analytics

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, sre-oncall@acmeanalytics.com
Date: 2026-10-03T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Debug access request: ephemeral logs for transaction failures

Evelyn / Lauren — forwarding a customer request. Acme needs a temporary retention exception to recover a trace for an ongoing production incident. They say they have signatures and only need read-only access to a 48-hour window.

Questions I have:
- What is our standard process for granting a short-lived retention hold for debugging?
- Who must approve (legal, compliance, eng) and how quickly can we act?
- Any operational guardrails (redaction, scoped access, audit logging) we must require before we hand over access?

We are sensitive here since the buffer can contain PII. Happy to coordinate the redaction and host a joint session to pull the minimal artifacts.

Can you advise and, if OK, provide wording we can send back to Acme and the steps to initiate a temporary hold?

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Exec — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, sre-oncall@acmeanalytics.com
Date: 2026-10-04T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Debug access request: ephemeral logs for transaction failures

Marcus — thanks for the flag. Short answer: we can grant an exception under a tight set of controls. Please note the following mandatory requirements before any retention override is executed: 

1) Written customer authorization that specifies exact time range and scope (Acme has provided access-request-form.pdf — that helps).
2) Legal sign-off on the redaction plan: which fields will be masked and a single point of contact for questions.
3) Scoped, time-limited, read-only access with multi-factor access for the engineer pulling data.
4) Engineering must capture an audit snapshot (who accessed, timestamp, query parameters) and submit it to compliance immediately after extraction.
5) Maximum exception window: 72 hours backfill; default approval to 48 hours unless escalated.
6) No data copying off-platform unless explicitly approved; if necessary, we require an encrypted transfer with DLP controls and an approved transfer request.

If you can confirm Acme will accept those constraints, I can approve administratively for a single 48-hour read-only extraction. Anything outside that requires Legal + Privacy review which will add ~2 business days.

Suggested reply to customer (paste-ready):

"Marcus / Maya — we can make a one-time, read-only exception to permit access to the specified ephemeral traces under the following conditions: (a) you confirm the exact UTC time range and that you accept Redwood's redaction checklist; (b) access will be limited to a named engineer with MFA and logged; (c) Redwood will provide an audit record of access; (d) the window is limited to 48 hours. Please acknowledge and return the signed access-request-form. Once we have that we will schedule extraction within the next business day."

I'll approve on my side once you attach the signed acknowledgment.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: sre-oncall@acmeanalytics.com
Date: 2026-10-05T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Debug access request: ephemeral logs for transaction failures

Thanks — operational note and next steps from infra:

- We can perform a read-only backfill for the specified 2026-10-02 08:00:00Z — 2026-10-02 20:00:00Z window. Needs Evelyn's go-ahead (recorded).
- Engineer assigned: Priya N. (infra-debug). She will connect via a Zoom recorded session with Acme's SRE and Marcus.
- Access method: temporary access token with role "ephemeral_readonly" scoped to the customer namespace. Token expires automatically after 48 hours.
- We will run automated PII redaction first (see internal checklist link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/incident-20261002). Manual redaction by Priya only if necessary, logged to Jira OPS-1129.
- Attachments: we received trace_segment_20261002.json (partial); please confirm Acme's signed acknowledgement (access-request-form.pdf) includes acceptance of no-off-platform copy.

Marcus — can you coordinate the Zoom time and ask Acme to confirm the exact UTC range in writing? Once Evelyn posts approval in this thread I will kick off the token provisioning and schedule the extraction.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference
